rv.q: It was barely reviewed prior to its transfer, but has been playing to sold-out, ovating houses from the word go.

It takes its place in a West End that is hosting a particularly adventurous season this spring and is trying to reach out to new audiences. Yes, I know ticket prices are too high, but they are cheaper for this show than most, and worth every penny. The title sounds gloomy, not to mention the set-up of six young Black men in search of therapy.
...gut punch of a show remains a beautiful piece of theatre for all audiences...

“For Black Boys,” with its didactic enumeration of societal ills, has the feel of a PowerPoint presentation; its bracing directness befits the urgency of its message, but as a piece of art it never quite transports us.
...is a testament to progress made, and a reminder of the progress still to be made.
A moving description of the challenges facing young Black men, told with energy and honesty.

One of the play’s strengths lies in its exploration of identity and the initial confrontation with what sets individuals apart in a world where comparison is prevalent. Through the characters’ stories, For Black Boys sheds light on the multifaceted experiences of black men, validating their struggles and triumphs.

cn.t: Critics praise this gut-punch exploration of Black male bonding as beautiful and generous theatre, though reception ranges from deeply moved to more measured appreciation.
